spec_match.rationale: Probes correctly for a LegacyNoInterfaceObject result interface: static surface checks plus live-instance inspection, with the silently-failing wrong recipe shown beside the right one.

interactive.rationale: Probe and live-inspection buttons work; in this headless session recognition fails not-allowed and the page says exactly that, labelled as a mic/engine availability problem.

edge_cases.rationale: Distinguishes unsupported from null-timing from mic-denied; documents the unmerged spec PR and absent flag honestly.

references.rationale: ChromeStatus and web-speech-api PR links present.

conformance.rationale: All 8 assertions report BLOCKED here — the honest state for checks that need a live recognition session; none fake a pass or fail.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Static probe ran (SpeechRecognition present, result interface correctly absent from window); live branch surfaced the real not-allowed error; console clean otherwise.

telemetry_health.rationale: Branch asserts use literal true with distinguishing ids — diagnosable but not falsifiable.

accessibility.rationale: Buttons named, result tables scoped, aria-live outputs, visible focus.

openQuestions.title: Exercise the live-result branch where a recognition backend exists
openQuestions.detail: This environment has no microphone/speech backend (error: not-allowed) and all 8 conformance checks are blocked. On a machine with on-device recognition, run the live inspection and record whether audioStartTime/audioEndTime appear on a real result (the attributes were not in Chromium main's IDL as of 2026-07-24 per the page's own note).

summary: Verified on headless Chromium 153 (Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12) driven over CDP via a Playwright script — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud environment; desktop 1280×800 and mobile 360×740 DPR3 screenshots captured and inspected. The probe teaches the correct detection recipe and degrades honestly without a speech backend.
